previous_disclosures.section: Results of Operations > Asset & Wealth Management > THE GOLDMAN SACHS GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES
previous_disclosures.summary: Assets Under Supervision (AUS) includes institutional clients' assets, assets sourced through third-party distributors, and high-net-worth clients' assets where the firm earns a fee for managing assets on a discretionary basis, including mutual funds, hedge funds, credit funds, private equity funds, real estate funds, and separately managed accounts. It also includes client assets invested with third-party managers, private bank deposits, and advisory relationships where the firm earns fees but does not have investment discretion, excluding self-directed brokerage assets. Liquidity products include money market funds and private bank deposits. Direct strategies primarily include private equity, growth equity, private credit, liquid alternatives, and real estate strategies. Alternative assets included $58 billion in uncalled capital as of December 2023. Non-fee-earning alternative assets primarily consist of balance sheet investments, unfunded commitments, and direct investing strategies like private equity and real estate. Equity securities included $12.1 billion in private equity positions and $1.1 billion in public equity positions (converted from private equity) as of December 2023.

comparisons.peer_topic: Wealth segment business definition and scope
comparisons.peer_summary: The Wealth segment comprises the Private Bank, Wealth at Work, and Citigold businesses, providing financial services such as banking, lending, and custody to affluent, high net worth, and ultra-high net worth clients across 20 countries including the U.S., Mexico, Singapore, Hong Kong, the UAE, and London.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies define their wealth management segments by the types of clients served and the scope of services provided, including high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth individuals. Goldman Sachs' Assets Under Supervision (AUS) definition covers institutional, third-party distributed, and high-net-worth client assets where the firm earns fees for discretionary management or advisory. Citi's Wealth segment similarly comprises businesses (Private Bank, Wealth at Work, Citigold) that provide financial services to affluent, high net worth, and ultra-high net worth clients. Both disclosures highlight the focus on fee-generating relationships with affluent client segments, although GS specifically categorizes by the nature of the asset supervision (discretionary/advisory) while Citi categorizes by client wealth tier and business unit.

sentences.text: AUS includes our institutional clients' assets, assets sourced through third-party distributors and high-net-worth clients' assets where we earn a fee for managing assets on a discretionary basis.
This includes net assets in our mutual funds, hedge funds, credit funds, private equity funds, real estate funds, and separately managed accounts for institutional and individual investors.

Wealth includes the Private Bank, Wealth at Work and Citigold businesses and provides financial services to a range of client segments including affluent, high net worth and ultra-high net worth clients through banking, lending, mortgages, investment, custody and trust product offerings in 20 countries, including the U.S., Mexico and four wealth management centers: Singapore, Hong Kong, the UAE and London.
Private Bank provides financial services to ultra-high net worth clients through customized product offerings.

comparisons.peer_topic: Wealth Management Asset Management Revenue Account Types
comparisons.peer_summary: Asset management revenues within the Wealth Management segment are primarily generated from six types of accounts: separately managed-accounts, unified managed-accounts, advisor-accounts, portfolio manager-accounts, and cash management-accounts.
comparisons.comparison: Both firms define the composition of their asset management offerings within Wealth Management, though MS provides a more granular breakdown of account types while GS focuses on the source of the assets (discretionary vs. advisory). Goldman Sachs defines Assets Under Supervision (AUS) to include assets where it has discretionary management authority or provides advisory services for which it earns a fee, explicitly excluding self-directed brokerage assets. Similarly, Morgan Stanley details the specific account structures that generate asset management revenue, such as Separately Managed Accounts (SMAs) where third-party or affiliated managers make investment decisions, and Unified Managed Accounts, which align with GS's inclusion of discretionary management. Both disclosures serve to define the scope of fee-generating managed assets within their respective wealth management segments.

sentences.text: AUS includes our institutional clients' assets, assets sourced through third-party distributors and high-net-worth clients' assets where we earn a fee for managing assets on a discretionary basis.
AUS does not include the self-directed brokerage assets of our clients.

• Separately managed-accounts by which third party and affiliated asset managers are engaged to manage clients' assets with investment decisions made by the asset manager. Only one third-party asset manager strategy can be held per account.
• Advisor-accounts where the investment decisions must be approved by the client, and the financial advisor must obtain approval each time a change is made to the account or its investments.
